justification.synthesis_rationale: Starting from a mid-range anchor of 0.60 based on pre-election polling, we incorporate updates from five causal factors that push probability up or down. While Greens regain some ground and late headlines show a narrowing lead, the convergence of multiple independent signals toward CDU ahead, and the mechanics of BW's 120-seat MMP system, yield a high posterior probability that CDU wins the most seats. Calibrated to reflect potential correlations among polls and market signals, the final estimate remains high but acknowledges residual uncertainty due to turnout effects and regional variances.

question: Will CDU win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?
summary: Ensemble aggregate strongly suggested CDU would win the most seats, but late-February polling reveals Greens closing the vote gap and introduces non-trivial seat-translation risk under BW's 120-seat MMP system.
The BW system can produce a larger Greens seat share than their statewide vote share would imply, meaning a CDU vote lead does not guarantee a CDU-seat lead.
Turnout uncertainty and undecided voters create potential last-minute swings toward Greens or anti-establishment options, reducing CDU's edge.
Prediction signals generally favor CDU first, but margins are tight and outcomes remain probabilistic.

justification.critique_assessment: The objections are valid and reveal real uncertainties about seat translation and turnout; none rely on physically implausible scenarios.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.91 to 0.70 to account for the non-negligible risks identified (greens closing the gap, MMP seat translation effects, turnout and late swing risks), yielding a calibrated but still favorable probability for CDU having the most seats.

forecasts.reference-class: Baden-Württemberg Landtag election (8 March 2026) using mixed-member proportional representation; base-rate derived from pre-election polls showing CDU ahead of Greens in Baden-Württemberg in February 2026.

sources.claim: Umfragen im Feb. 2026 zeigen CDU vor Grün, z. B. CDU ca. 27–29% und Grüne ca. 19–25% (je nach Institut).
Polls in early 2026 place the CDU in the lead in Baden-Württemberg with Greens in the low- to mid-20s across multiple surveys.
SWP reports a poll where CDU around 29%, Greens around 23%, AfD around 20%, suggesting CDU holds a lead.
Polymarket Grok Prediction: Greens as the second-largest group with ~70% probability; implies CDU would have the most seats.
ZDF Politbarometer Extra (Feb 2026, 23–26 Feb) shows CDU ahead in Baden-Württemberg according to the polling window.
DPA report (Oct 2025) indicates CDU lead narrowing but still ahead; Özdemir leads minister-president.
Infratest dimap poll (Jan 22, 2026): CDU 29.0%, Greens 23.0%, AfD 20.0%, SPD 8.0%, Linke 7.0%, FDP 5.0%, Others 8.0%.
Insa poll (early Feb 2026): Greens 22%, CDU 28% (gap of 6 points); AfD 20%, SPD 10%, Linke 7%, FDP 6%.
INSA (Oct 2025) reported CDU around 31% and Greens around 17%; Infratest dimap for SWR/Stuttgarter Zeitung showed CDU ~29% and Greens ~20%.
Overview of latest BW polls: Infratest dimap CDU ~29%, Greens ~23%; INSA CDU ~29%, Greens ~21% (Feb 2026 data, multiple polls).
Kretschmann cautions Greens on poll results; latest polls show CDU in the lead with around 29% and Greens around 20%.
ARD Vorwahlumfrage (Feb 23–25, 2026): CDU 28%, Grüne 27%, AfD 18%, SPD 7%, FDP 6%, Die Linke 5%.
Insa-Umfrage (Feb 17–23, 2026): CDU 28%, Grüne 22% (Grüne holen auf, CDU bleibt stärkste Kraft).
Swp/ZDF-Insa-Trend: Grüne schließen Abstand; CDU bleibt vorne, aber Vorsprung schmilzt.
Zeit (Oct 2025): CDU 26–33%, Grüne rund 20% (Spannung vor der Landtagswahl am 8. März 2026).
Infografik (Feb 26, 2026): Infratest dimap poll with CDU around 28% and Grüne around 27%.
Welt (Feb 2026): Insa-Umfrage zeigt CDU 28%, Grüne 22% – Kopf-an-Kopf-Rennen möglich.

causal-factors.name: Poll lead margin for CDU vs Greens (late Feb 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple late-Feb polls show CDU ahead around 28–29% with Greens generally in the low- to mid-20s, sustaining a lead that supports CDU having the most seats under BW's proportional system.

causal-factors.name: Greens closing gap relative to CDU in some polls
causal-factors.rationale: Insa and other polls show Greens near the low-20s while CDU remains in the high-20s, narrowing the lead and raising the risk CDU would not win the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets indicate CDU-first scenario (Greens second)
causal-factors.rationale: Polymarket suggests Greens as second-largest with around 70% probability, implying CDU would have the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Expert polling and media coverage corroborate CDU lead in Feb 2026
causal-factors.rationale: ZDF Politbarometer Extra and INSA/Infra polls in Feb 2026 show CDU ahead—consistent with CDU as the largest party in votes and seat counts.

causal-factors.name: Lead narrows over time in earlier forecasts (Oct 2025–Feb 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: Earlier forecasts indicated a narrowing lead with Greens potentially closing the gap, signaling ongoing uncertainty about CDU securing the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Sustained CDU lead in late-February polls
causal-factors.rationale: Polls in late February 2026 show CDU around 28% and Greens around 27% (Infratest dimap/ARD), indicating CDU still leads but by a narrow margin.

causal-factors.name: Greens closing the gap and potential for Greens to overtake in some polls
causal-factors.rationale: Greens have been gaining ground in several polls (e.g., INSA 22% Greens vs CDU 28%; ARD 27% Greens), narrowing CDU's lead.

causal-factors.name: Kretschmann not running; Greens lose incumbency advantage
causal-factors.rationale: Winfried Kretschmann will not seek re-election in 2026, potentially eroding Green incumbency advantages and aiding CDU.

causal-factors.name: Seat distribution under BW's 120-seat system supports CDU lead in current projections
causal-factors.rationale: Infratest dimap projections cited via PolitPro show CDU around 36 seats vs Greens around 28 (out of 120), suggesting CDU would hold a seat lead if votes hold.

causal-factors.name: Endgame turnout and last-week swing uncertainty
causal-factors.rationale: ARD poll indicates a meaningful share of voters are undecided or could shift close to election, creating potential late swings.

causal-factors.name: Cross-poll variations across institutes
causal-factors.rationale: Different pollsters show CDU/Greens margins varying (CDU 28–29% vs Greens 22–27%), signaling uncertain final margins.

causal-factors.name: Polls show CDU ahead late Feb 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple polls conducted around Feb 23–26, 2026 (e.g., INSA, infratest dimap/ARD, ZDF window) place CDU ahead of Greens by roughly 2–6 percentage points in Baden-Württemberg, boosting the likelihood CDU wins the most seats. causal-factors.name: AfD remains around 18–20%, complicating outcomes
causal-factors.rationale: AfD sustaining roughly 18–20% across polls reduces CDU’s margin and increases coalition dynamics that could limit CDU’s sole hold on Most Seats. ([fr.de](https://www.fr.de/politik/landtagswahl-in-baden-wuerttemberg-umfragen-mit-prognose-fuer-ergebnis-94056774.html?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Seat translation under BW's mixed-member proportional system
causal-factors.rationale: Under BW's 120-seat MMP system, final seat counts can diverge from vote shares, keeping some scenarios where CDU does not secure the clear majority even if leading in polls. ([fr.de](https://www.fr.de/politik/landtagswahl-in-baden-wuerttemberg-umfragen-mit-prognose-fuer-ergebnis-94056774.html?utm_source=openai))

synthesis: The CDU leading in polls and the ensemble projection remain plausible but are tempered by known risks from the Baden-Württemberg MMP system, Greens momentum, and turnout dynamics. Calibrated probability is set to 0.70 with a balanced range reflecting plausible variation.
